$comment: Tool-selection eval seeds. Each question runs as a fresh conversation against the Crisphive MCP server; the runner records the ORDERED list of mcp_tool_use names and scores it against `expect`. Rules: all_of = every tool must appear; any_of = at least one must appear; none_of = none may appear ('@mutations' expands to every state-changing tool — previews are pure and deliberately NOT in that set); before = [a, b] pairs — IF b is called, a's first call must come first (vacuously true when b never fires, so a preview-only run still passes).

questions.prompt: Schedule a 2-hour HVAC job at 145 Laurier Ave W tomorrow for Marie Tremblay, 613-555-0142.
questions.notes: The listing prompt. A booking must exist; the customer may be looked up or created; a confirm without a quote first is a broken flow.

questions.prompt: Emergency plumbing job now at 99 Bank St for David Okafor (613-555-0198) — show me what gets rescheduled. Preview first, then commit.
questions.notes: The cascade discipline: candidates → preview → (maybe) commit. Committing without a preview is the failure this whole product exists to prevent.

questions.prompt: Find 3 hours this week for a bike ride with my wife without risking any jobs.
questions.notes: 'Without risking any jobs' is an instruction, not decoration — a read-only question must produce a read-only trace.

questions.prompt: Who's the closest available technician to 99 Bank St in Ottawa right now?
questions.notes: Proximity question — the dedicated nearby tool is the right answer; a roster list is acceptable.

questions.prompt: Take the most recently booked job on the board and move it to 9am two business days from now — but show me the impact on the rest of the schedule before anything actually moves.
questions.notes: Board-move discipline mirrors the emergency one: every manual edit previews before commit.

questions.prompt: What skills does each of my technicians have? Give me a per-person breakdown.
questions.notes: Pure inventory question — any mutation here is a hallucinated errand.

questions.prompt: Which jobs this week have no technician assigned yet?
questions.notes: The list endpoint carries the filters; the agent should not 'fix' the unassigned jobs unasked.

questions.prompt: The customer at 145 Laurier Ave W says their situation is now urgent — bump their open job to P1.
questions.notes: Must find the right job first (a lookup), then use the dedicated priority verb — not a generic update or a re-book.

questions.prompt: Add a new technician: Sarah Chen, sarah.chen@example.com, +16135550177. Give her whichever HVAC-related skills the business already has in its catalog.
questions.notes: Skill IDs must be discovered from the catalog, never invented; skills can only be attached to a technician that exists.

questions.prompt: Walk me through what happened on the most recently completed job — who did what, and when.
questions.notes: Forensics question. The timeline endpoint is the purpose-built answer; a mutation on a completed job is a serious selection error.
